records.region: Southern Texas, United States: San Diego–Alice–Pintas–Petronila and the Alazan Bay coastal setting
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded mapped downstream creek candidate; not a completed representative identity for the entire selection.
records.material_pending_reason: The long final southeastward extension from the estuarine corridor across intervening land/wetland beside Cayo Hinosa and across the peninsula north of Alazan Bay to the actual selected endpoint. No selected through-channel or specified generalized aquatic connection is established.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected middle course uses the mapped Pintas connection from the San Fernando setting to Petronila. It does not continue south along San Fernando toward Kingsville or use the separate Agua Dulce/Banquete headwater approach. The actual final endpoint lies in the peninsula land/wetland setting north of Alazan Bay; a familiar coastal name is not substituted for that ending.
records.completion_scope: All 21 selected parts and the actual endpoint were visually considered in five original USGSTopo views. The San Diego–San Fernando–Pintas–Petronila corridors and joins are supported; the long final land/wetland extension north of Alazan Bay remains unresolved.
records.supported_name_scope: Local named-channel correspondence is supported for San Diego Creek, San Fernando Creek, Pintas Creek and Petronila Creek. Distinct reach names are compatible with a representative-system assessment; they are not themselves the reason this record remains pending.

scope_limits: The selected northwestern opening is a point on the mapped San Diego Creek, not a verified natural source.
The mapped San Fernando–Pintas connection supports geographic correspondence, but its natural/managed character, current operation and flow distribution are unverified.
Intermittent linework, pools, side lakes and tidal water polygons do not establish perennial flow or present water level.
Cayo Hinosa is a directly observed reference-map label, not a verified formal registry spelling or an assigned name for the entire selected terminal extension.
The terminal gap is wider than an individual bank/vertex mismatch; the selected long extension crosses intervening land/wetland and no selected through-connection is established.

records.region: Northern Baffin Island, Nunavut, Canada; Jungersen River–Jungersen Bay corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the connected selected eastern feeder and Jungersen River corridor to Jungersen Bay. The initial unlabelled feeder and minor links are not assigned a uniform scalar river name.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system research using the retained permitted field-study maps and prose. No selected-route through-link remains materially unresolved at ordinary regional/corridor scale. Accepted names remain null and all application flags remain false.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected selected eastern feeder and Jungersen River corridor to Jungersen Bay. The initial unlabelled feeder and minor links are not assigned a uniform scalar river name.

naming_scope_details.unnamed_components: The initial eastern feeder and minor connecting reaches have no separately established names in this pass.
naming_scope_details.no_unnamed_claim: An unestablished component name does not mean that no Inuit, local or official name exists.

records.material_pending_reason: The chosen inland opening, intervening river/lake parts and joins, and the final selected branch into a receiving waterbody remain unestablished by the available original material.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No supported river-name candidate for the selected northern Victoria Island corridor. Richard Collinson Inlet is a coastal receiving-water lead only, not a candidate river name or an established selected terminal connection.
records.completion_scope: All 22 selected parts were considered in six geographic components. Original ARC403 coastal prose and its chapter overview support regional Richard Collinson Inlet context only; no inland route or actual selected terminal branch correspondence was completed.
records.supported_name_scope: No supported river-name candidate for the selected northern Victoria Island corridor. Richard Collinson Inlet is a coastal receiving-water lead only, not a candidate river name or an established selected terminal connection.

scope_limits: None of the selected inland opening, part-to-part joins, potential lake/glacial passages or lower main-channel approaches has complete independently read correspondence.
The braided stream described at the head of Richard Collinson Inlet is a regional lead, not proof that the selected ending follows it or that the selected river has any particular name.
Absence of a supported candidate does not mean the river lacks a current local, Indigenous or official name.

Historical generic NLUIS series identity did not independently establish the proposed Saneraun Hills87H and Richard Collinson Inlet88A publication relationship; their inferred normal-original URLs were not requested.
No precise bank, modern flow, surveyed endpoint, or single scalar name across every selected component is demanded. The remaining gaps concern ordinary route and terminal correspondence.

records.material_pending_reason: The western opening, northern loop, subsequent southeastern lowland links and waterbody passages, and the actual internal terminal are not established. The regional Colorada Grande salina label is not assigned to the selected endpoint.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative river-system or reach name is established. Salina Colorada Grande is retained only as a regional waterbody name, not an assigned river name or a confirmed receiving endpoint.
records.completion_scope: All 43 selected parts were considered in six components. The university geography book supplies regional valley and salina context, but does not establish the selected path or its actual terminal.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative river-system or reach name is established. Salina Colorada Grande is retained only as a regional waterbody name, not an assigned river name or a confirmed receiving endpoint.

scope_limits: The complete selected course may include diffuse drainage, discontinuous channels, saline depressions or modeled links, but the acquired evidence does not classify each interval.
A named nearby or regional salina does not provide a name for the selected river or prove the actual endpoint.
The missing evidence is ordinary corridor/through-link correspondence, not exact bank positions, individual vertices or present flow/management conditions.
No whole-system scalar name, formal registry match or Korean name is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
